correctness_confidence.basis: All main theorems and corollaries check out rigorously from first principles: Courant-Fischer generalized Rayleigh bounds in Thm 2.1, Young-identity optimization and 4x4 block-limit sharpness in Thm 3.1, 3-case Cheeger bound and 2x2 rift in Thm 4.1, and reverse-triangle localization plus equipartite classification and K_{4,4}+e minimization in Thm 5.1.

rigor.basis: Proofs are concise, self-contained, and carefully handle boundary cases (2-lambda_n=0, S=0, orthogonal complement eigenspaces, axis of symmetry checks). Minor looseness: Eq. (18) calls P(t) quadratic even at lambda=2/r (r>=3) where it degenerates to linear (uniqueness still holds via P'<0), Abstract item 1 drops a denominator, and Table 1 Row 6 lists Alon-Boppana under sharp families.

novelty.basis: Establishes genuinely original quantitative laws for the spectral Braess paradox, notably the size-independent d-degeneracy immunity floor 1 - sqrt(d/(d+r)), the asymmetric Cheeger-spectral rift below (r+s)/(r+s+2), and the K_{4,4}+e regular minimum. Techniques are clean elementary linear algebra, Young inequalities, and equitable quotients combined with known spectral bounds.

significance.basis: Resolves exact worst-case degradation ratios for lambda_2, 2-lambda_n, and gamma_* across four fundamental regimes with matching extremal families, sharply separating sparse bounded-degeneracy perturbations from dense clique/biclique saboteurs. Regular-graph sharpness for lambda_2<1 and exact planar/outerplanar immunity constants remain open.

reproducibility.basis: Provides closed-form expressions, explicit extremal families, and a Table 2 SHA-256 verification ledger referencing Lean 4.36.0 and Python test scripts. However, Lean formalizes only 15 algebraic/inequality lemmas rather than the full spectral-graph theorems, and external artifacts were not inspected in this PDF-only assessment.

summary: This paper establishes exact quantitative laws governing how adding an edge-disjoint subgraph H to a connected non-complete graph G (minimum degree r >= 1) degrades the normalized Laplacian spectral gap lambda_2, bipartiteness gap 2-lambda_n, and absolute spectral gap gamma_*. Theorem 2.1 proves the universal multiplicative Weyl bound 1/(1 + rho(D_G^{-1/2} A_H D_G^{-1/2})) >= r/(r + rho(A_H)), which pairs with Stanley's and Nosal-Nikiforov's bounds to identify cliques K_t and bicliques K_{a,a} as asymptotically sharp k-edge saboteurs on K_{r,m}. Theorem 3.1 proves the Degeneracy Immunity Theorem: any d-degenerate H of arbitrary size and maximum degree obeys the sharp size-independent floor 1 - sqrt(d/(d+r)) (achieved by K_{r,m}+K_{d,k}), with a lambda-refinement approaching r/(r+2d). Theorem 4.1 proves the Cheeger floor (r+s)/(r+s+2) for a single edge between degrees r != s alongside a tighter 2x2 spectral floor Psi(r,s;lambda), establishing a strict Cheeger-spectral rift realized by G_{r,s,M}. Theorem 5.1 establishes a regular-graph localization barrier > r/(r+1) via Alon-Boppana, classifies lambda_2=1 regular graphs as K_{m,...,m}, and proves K_{4,4}+e gives the unique global minimum (14-sqrt(26))/10. All mathematical proofs hold rigorously.
strengths: Clean, airtight Courant-Fischer proof of the Universal Multiplicative Weyl Inequality (Theorem 2.1) covering all lambda_j(G) <= 1, 2-lambda_n(G), and gamma_*(G), paired with exact asymptotic sharpness via K_{r,m}+K_t and K_{r,m}+K_{a,a} (Corollary 2.2).

Genuinely surprising Degeneracy Immunity Theorem (Theorem 3.1): a parameterized Young-type square identity along bounded-out-degree acyclic orientations yields the exact size-independent floor 1-sqrt(d/(d+r)) and matching extremal family K_{r,m}+K_{d,k}.

Rigorous resolution of the Asymmetric Single-Edge Law (Theorem 4.1), establishing a strict four-level Cheeger-spectral rift for r != s via exact 2x2 reduction Psi(r,s;lambda) and explicit clique-attachment witnesses G_{r,s,M}.

Complete classification of lambda_2=1 connected non-complete r-regular graphs as K_{m,...,m}, strict optimality of K_{r,r}+e for r >= 3, and exact algebraic global minimum (14-sqrt(26))/10 at K_{4,4}+e alongside the lambda_2 < 1 localization obstruction (Theorem 5.1).
Transparent scope separation between algebraic/inequality lemmas certified in Lean 4.36.0 and full spectral/asymptotic proofs, plus clear open problems.
weaknesses: Proof techniques are mostly elementary spectral and quadratic methods (Rayleigh quotients, Cauchy-Schwarz, Young's identity, equitable 3x3/4x4 quotients) combined with known spectral bounds (Stanley, Nosal-Nikiforov, Alon-Boppana).
Sharpness is established only for k=C(t,2) and k=a^2 in Corollary 2.2, and only at lambda_2=1 in Theorem 3.1 (not for the lambda-refined bound 1/C(r,d;lambda) when lambda < 1) and Theorem 5.1(b).

The regular localization bound Phi_reg(r,lambda) in Theorem 5.1(a) is not proven sharp for lambda_2 < 1 (e.g., at r=2 it gives 0.80 while C_n+e approaches 1), and Table 1 Row 6 misleadingly lists Alon-Boppana under Sharp Extremal Family.

Minor editorial/technical slips: Abstract item 1 omits the denominator /(2-lambda_n(G)) in prose, and Theorem 5.1(a)'s proof calls P(t) quadratic even at lambda=2/r (r>=3) where it degenerates to linear (though uniqueness in (0,1) still holds via P'<0).
Exact immunity constants for outerplanar (K_{2,3}-free) and planar (K_{3,3}-free) subgraphs remain open, and Lean 4 covers only 15 algebraic helper lemmas rather than the full matrix spectral proofs.
strong_novelty_candidates: Universal Multiplicative Weyl Inequality (Theorem 2.1): 1/(1 + rho(D_G^{-1/2} A_H D_G^{-1/2})) >= r/(r+rho(A_H)) holding uniformly for lambda_j <= 1, 2-lambda_n, and gamma_*, yielding sharp clique and biclique saboteur optimality.

Exact Degeneracy Immunity Theorem (Theorem 3.1): sharp size- and degree-independent lower bound 1 - sqrt(d/(d+r)) (and lambda-refinement 1/C(r,d;lambda)) for all d-degenerate subgraphs H, with matching extremal family K_{r,m}+K_{d,k}.

Asymmetric Single-Edge Law and Cheeger-Spectral Rift (Theorem 4.1): exact 2x2 spectral floor Psi(r,s;lambda) breaking strictly below the universal Cheeger conductance floor (r+s)/(r+s+2) whenever r != s, witnessed by G_{r,s,M}.

Regular-Graph Localization Obstruction and K_{4,4}+e Global Minimum (Theorem 5.1): strict barrier Phi_reg(r,lambda) > r/(r+1) for lambda_2 < 1, complete equipartite classification at lambda_2=1, and unique global minimum (14-sqrt(26))/10 at K_{4,4}+e.
